payload.statement_nl: For every real number x, 0 ≤ x - floor(x).

result_payload.addressed_previous_feedback: The revised proof stays strictly within the floor-function inequality floor(x) ≤ x and does not invoke any unsupported fractional-part identity or unrelated theorem.
result_payload.proof_nl: Fix any real number x. By the definition of the floor function, floor(x) is the greatest integer less than or equal to x; in particular, floor(x) ≤ x. Subtracting floor(x) from both sides gives x - floor(x) ≥ 0. Since x was arbitrary, this holds for every real number x. Hence, for all real x, 0 ≤ x - floor(x).
result_payload.proof_summary: Use the defining property of the floor function: floor(x) ≤ x. Rearranging immediately yields x - floor(x) ≥ 0 for every real x.
